messages.author: 5c600e01882cd5a1
messages.subject: Uploaded files temporary or permanent?
parts: I have a Shiny app deployed on shipyapps.io which allows users to upload .csv's. What happens to the user's file afterwards? Is it saved somewhere permanently? Temporarily, and erased after the session? Thanks!

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Uploaded files temporary or permanent?
parts: You should assume that the files will be lost since the files that are being uploaded will be written to temporary storage (unless you do something like put them in a more permanent data store, or we provide persistent storage as part of the platform).  That temporary storage essentially goes away when the application goes to sleep for lack of usage, and comes back clean when it starts up again.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Uploaded files temporary or permanent?
parts:
Tareef,

Just hopping onto this thread as I have been asked this question a few times.

Can you please clarify your file retention policy? Does the temp storage get deleted eg when the user closes the application or refreshes the browser, or does it persist if other users are using the application elsewhere? Does it delete when the instance the user was accessing shuts down or all instances of the app have shut down?

Would be great to have some kind of official explanation I could point app users to as this gets asked a lot.

Thanks

Mark

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Uploaded files temporary or permanent?
parts:
Hi Mark,
Our retention policy is likely to change when we introduce persistent storage but as of today the storage on the instance you are running with will be around for as long as that application instance is up.  Recall that you can have multiple instances for a given application and so the storage is tied to the application instance today.  
My recommendation for folks who care about making sure that their content is truly transient, is to write the files that are uploaded to /tmp.   That /tmp directory will be clean every time the application instance gets restarted for whatever reason.  Alternatively, you could register a handler on the session in the onSessionEnded to handle any cleanup you want to do.  Here is the link to the documentation for that.  

Hope this helps.
-Tareef
